title: Residue Assignment
content: A `ResidueAssignment x` is a function assigning to each prime $p \leq x$ a residue class $a_p$. The assignment determines which integers each prime 'covers': prime $p$ covers $n$ when $n \equiv a_p \pmod{p}$.

mathContext.leanSignature: def ResidueAssignment (x : ℕ) := (p : ℕ) → p.Prime → p ≤ x → ℕ
mathContext.proofTechnique: dependent function type over primes ≤ x
mathContext.formalizationNote: Uses dependent types to restrict to primes ≤ x. The residue is a natural number; congruence is checked via `n % p = a % p`.

title: Prime Partition Structure
content: A `PrimePartition x` partitions primes $\leq x$ into sets $A$ and $B$ via a Boolean classifier `inA`. Both sets must be non-empty (witnessed by existential proofs).

mathContext.latex: \{p \leq x : p \text{ prime}\} = A \sqcup B,\quad A \neq \emptyset,\, B \neq \emptyset
mathContext.leanSignature: structure PrimePartition (x : ℕ) where inA : (p : ℕ) → p.Prime → p ≤ x → Bool; nonemptyA : ...; nonemptyB : ...
mathContext.formalizationNote: Uses `Bool` for the classifier rather than `Prop`, enabling computation. The non-emptiness fields are existential proofs.

title: Coverage and Dual Covering
content: Defines `CoveredByA`, `CoveredByB`, and `IsDualCovering`. An integer $n$ is covered by $A$ if $\exists p \in A,\, n \equiv a_p \pmod{p}$. A dual covering requires every $n < x$ is covered by both $A$ and $B$ independently.

mathContext.latex: \text{IsDualCovering} :\Leftrightarrow \forall n < x,\, (\exists p \in A,\, n \equiv a_p) \wedge (\exists q \in B,\, n \equiv a_q)
mathContext.leanSignature: def IsDualCovering (x : ℕ) (assign : ResidueAssignment x) (part : PrimePartition x) : Prop := ∀ n : ℕ, n < x → CoveredByA x assign part n ∧ CoveredByB x assign part n
mathContext.proofTechnique: universal quantification with conjunction of two coverage conditions

title: Main Conjecture: Erdős Problem 467
content: For all sufficiently large $x$, there exist a residue assignment and a prime partition achieving dual coverage. The problem asks whether the redundancy in prime residue classes ($\sum 1/p$ diverges) is enough to split primes into two halves that each cover everything.

mathContext.latex: \exists X,\, \forall x \geq X,\, \exists (a_p)_{p \leq x},\, \exists A \sqcup B,\, \text{IsDualCovering}(x)
mathContext.leanSignature: axiom erdos_467_conjecture : ∃ X : ℕ, ∀ x : ℕ, x ≥ X → ∃ assign : ResidueAssignment x, ∃ part : PrimePartition x, IsDualCovering x assign part
mathContext.proofTechnique: existential statement — asks for construction or probabilistic existence
mathContext.designChoices: Axiomatized since the problem is open. The quantifier structure (∃X, ∀x≥X, ∃assign, ∃part) carefully captures 'for sufficiently large x'.

title: Residue Class Properties (Proved)
content: Seven fully proved basic properties: $n \bmod p < p$, $n \bmod p = 0 \iff p \mid n$, $n \bmod 2 \in \{0,1\}$, residue periodicity $(a + kp) \bmod p = a \bmod p$, every $n \geq 2$ has a prime factor, prime factors are $\leq n$, and for $n < x$ prime factors are $\leq x$.

mathContext.latex: n \bmod p < p,\quad n \bmod p = 0 \iff p \mid n
mathContext.proofTechnique: direct application of Nat.mod, Nat.dvd, and Nat.minFac lemmas
mathContext.formalizationNote: All seven results are fully proved with no sorry.

title: Zero Assignment Analysis (Proved)
content: The zero assignment $a_p = 0$ for all $p$ is fully analyzed: $n = 0$ is covered by every prime, $n = 1$ is never covered (no prime divides 1), and every $n \geq 2$ is covered via its smallest prime factor. The equivalence `zero_assign_cover_iff`: coverage by $p$ iff $p \mid n$.

mathContext.leanSignature: def zeroAssignment (x : ℕ) : ResidueAssignment x := fun _ _ _ => 0
mathContext.formalizationNote: Shows single-set coverage is easy for $n \geq 2$ using all primes. The dual coverage challenge is splitting primes so both halves independently cover.

title: Partition and Dual Covering Properties (Proved)
content: Six fully proved structural results. `dual_implies_A/B_covers`: projections. `dual_covering_double_hit`: every $n < x$ is hit by $\geq 2$ primes (one from each side). `partition_uses_two_primes`: $\geq 2$ primes required. `partition_has_distinct_labels`: $A \neq B$. `partition_needs_prime`: $x \geq 2$ necessary.

mathContext.latex: \text{IsDualCovering} \implies \forall n < x,\, \exists p \in A,\, \exists q \in B
mathContext.proofTechnique: direct decomposition of conjunction and existential witnesses
mathContext.formalizationNote: All six results are fully proved. `dual_covering_double_hit` is the key structural lemma.

title: Residue Class Periodicity (Proved)
content: Three proved results: $(n + p) \bmod p = n \bmod p$ (periodicity), $a < p \implies a \bmod p = a$ (identity in range), and $n \bmod p < p$ (range bound). These establish that each residue class covers exactly $1/p$ fraction of integers.

title: CRT for Distinct Primes
content: For distinct primes $p, q$ and any residues $a, b$, the Chinese Remainder Theorem guarantees $\exists n,\, n \equiv a \pmod{p} \wedge n \equiv b \pmod{q}$. Axiomatized; provable from `ZMod.chineseRemainder`. CRT implies coverage events from distinct primes are independent.

mathContext.latex: p \neq q \text{ prime} \implies \forall a, b,\, \exists n,\, n \equiv a \pmod{p} \wedge n \equiv b \pmod{q}
mathContext.leanSignature: axiom crt_for_primes (p q a b : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (hq : q.Prime) (hne : p ≠ q) : ∃ n, n % p = a % p ∧ n % q = b % q
mathContext.formalizationNote: CRT implies independence: the probability of avoiding coverage by coprime moduli is $\prod (1 - 1/p)$.

title: Mertens-type Estimate
content: By Mertens' third theorem, $\prod_{p \leq x} (1 - 1/p) \sim e^{-\gamma}/\log x$, where $\gamma \approx 0.5772$ is the Euler-Mascheroni constant. This bounds the 'uncovered probability' — the fraction of integers not hit by any prime's residue class. For dual coverage, both $A$ and $B$ need enough primes that $\prod_{p \in A} (1 - 1/p)$ is small enough.

references: Hardy–Wright, An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers
mathContext.formalizationNote: The axiom statement is incomplete — it only asserts positivity rather than the full Mertens asymptotic. A complete formalization would need the Euler-Mascheroni constant.
